At the bell Pell went in front and soon had the race in hand, but Lucas was now feeling that fast first lap, and although overtaking Poole of Blackheath, he was unable to gain any further places.

Positions and times of our runners were:—2, Bedford, 30.20; 3, Walker, 30.35; Poole, 30.56; 6, Bishop, A., 31.35; 8, England, 32.8; 13, Woodhead, 32.45; 15, Lacey, J., 32.49; 16, Saville, 33.6; 17, Cuff, 33.13; 24, Laing, 34.40; 26, Savage, 34.42; 28, Taylor, A.

The next promotion in 1897, organised by Polytechnic Harriers, had at least two Belgrave competitors, Miles, who was sixth, and Poole, 7th, and the third open race over this course was held in 1903 when the now defunct Hairdressers’ A.C. were the promoting body.

There was a very keen race for the first three places between Poole (Worcester), Hutchison (Met) and Hawkins (Met) who eventually finished in that order, whilst Eric Hall, continuing his form finished 5th.
236 lined up for the start and Vickers and Hall were seen to be well placed shortly afterwards behind Hardy, Coleman, Hawkins, Poole and others.

Although we just missed a place in the scratch team event, Eric Hall walked exceedingly well to finish in fourth position behind three really first class walkers in Hawkins, Coleman and Poole on a course which is probably the fastest one in the south.
Hawkins, Poole and Huthison set a fast pace from the start with our Eric running well behind them. In next position came yours truly smothered from top to toe in grease.
He gradually increased this and at 15 k.metres was 1m.23s. in front of Coleman, going on to finish the course in 1h. 37m.34s with Coleman 1.39.46 and Poole 1.40.31.
